questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Explain the paradox of thrift

answer.exemplar: When everyone saves more, aggregate demand falls, reducing income so total saving may not rise; individually rational thrift becomes collectively harmful.

questions.explanation: Higher saving reduces spending and income. The paradox shows individual and collective outcomes can conflict.

questions.stem: Explain how MPC determines the spending multiplier

answer.exemplar: The spending multiplier equals 1 divided by MPS, or 1 over (1 minus MPC), so a higher MPC means a larger multiplier and more rounds of spending.

questions.explanation: Multiplier equals 1 over MPS. Higher MPC means less leakage, so each round of spending is larger.

questions.stem: Explain the balanced budget multiplier

answer.exemplar: The balanced budget multiplier is 1: equal increases in government spending and taxes raise GDP by the same amount, because spending enters directly.

questions.explanation: Equal changes in G and T yield a net multiplier of 1. Spending enters GDP directly while taxes only reduce consumption partially.
